THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondent.

This appeal is directed by against the impugned judgment and award in MVC.No.136/2016 by the Learned Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Madikeri dated 16.02.2018, whereby the appellant herein was awarded a compensation of Rs.3,25,000/- towards injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
2. The appellant-petitioner met with an accident on 05.05.2016 at 10.00 a.m while proceeding in the motorcycle.
The car bearing no.KA-21-MC-3313 came in a NC: 2023:KHC:20641 rash and negligent manner and collided with the motor cycle of the petitioner.

As a result, petitioner fell down and he sustained injuries and shifted to government hospital, Somwarpet and there after he was shifted to Sullia Medical Hospital and there after he was shifted to Yenopoya Medical Hospital, Mangalore.
He took treatment as inpatient upto to 20.06.2016 from the date of the accident.
It is contended that petitioner is still im- mobilised and due to accidental injuries his income has been impaired.

The petitioner contended that he was working as writer cum driver with PW-3 who was contractor, on daily wages earning Rs.600/- per day and due to accidental injuries he has been disabled from working.
It is contended that adequate compensation be granted to him considering the nature of injuries sustained by him.
3. On issuance of notice, the petitioner and the insurer of the offending car appeared before the Tribunal and owner of the car-respondent no.1 did not file any NC: 2023:KHC:20641 objections.

Respondent no.2 - insurance company contended that compensation claimed is exorbitant,
imaginary and untenable in law and that the owner of the car-respondent no.1 had violated the terms and conditions of the policy and as such the petition is liable to be dismissed against respondent no.2.

sentences.text: The Tribunal framed necessary issues and petitioner was examined as PW-1, two witnesses on his behalf were examined as PW-2 and PW-3, and Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-187 were marked in evidence.
The doctor who treated the petitioner was examined as CW-1 and four documents were marked through him as Ex.C-1 to Ex.C-4.
No evidence was led on behalf of the respondent no.2, but the copy of the policy was marked as Ex.R-1 by consent.

5. After hearing both the sides, the tribunal came to conclusion that the petitioner is entitled for a compensation of Rs.3,75,000/- under following heads:
Compensation Sl.No.
Nature of the heads amount NC: 2023:KHC:20641 1. Pain and suffering Rs.30,000=00 2. Loss and future income Rs.1,53,000=00 3.
Medical expenses Rs.1,00,000=00 Loss of income during laid up 4. Rs.12,000=00 period and rest period Conveyance/traveling
5. attendant nutritious food Rs.20,000=00 charges 6.
Total discomfort and loss of Rs.10,000=00 amenities 7.
Future medication Total Rs.3,25,000=00 6.

Subsequent to passing of the judgment a review petition was filed by the respondent no.2-insurance company and by virtue of the order of the said review petition, medical expenses awarded by the Tribunal came to be reduced by Rs.50,000/- and the total compensation amount was restricted to Rs.3,25,000/-.
7. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner is before this court in appeal.
8. On issuance of notice by this court, respondent no.2-insurance company has appeared through its NC: 2023:KHC:20641 counsel.
Notice to respondent no.1 is dispensed with, as per the memo filed by the counsel for the appellant.
9. The trial court records have been secured and the arguments of both sides are heard.
10. The learned counsel for the appellant has filed I.A.No.2/2019 seeking production of additional documents in the matter.

It was contended in the affidavit filed in support of application that the appellant had appeared before the Medical Board, District Hospital which issued disability certificate pursuant to which the Tahsildar has also issued disability certificate entitling the appellant herein to receive the eligible facilities from the government.

It was contended that disability certificate indicate that there is disability of 50% and therefore those documents which M. M. Usman vs K. K. Ibrahim on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56654915/
3 have come into existence after impugned judgment, are necessary to be produced as additional evidence.

sentences.text: The Respondent no.2-insurance company though has not filed any objections to the said application, the learned counsel has orally opposed the NC: 2023:KHC:20641 same contending that said documents are not relevant at this juncture since the appellant had not produced those documents before the Tribunal when he was given an opportunity to adduce the evidence.
11. It is relevant to note that an application under order 41 rule 27 of CPC can be entertained only if the conditions which are enshrined in the rule 27 are satisfied.
The satisfaction in respect of the requirement of the additional evidence is to be felt by the court and it cannot be sought as of right by the appellant or any other party.
Now the question, is whether the documents produced by the appellant are essential for the purpose of the just decision in the matter.
Obviously, the appellant-petitioner had produced the disability certificate issued by the CW-1 and also had adduced evidence before the Tribunal.

It is evident that subsequent to the judgment passed by the Tribunal,
the appellant has obtained a certificate allegedly from the medical board of the district hospital which has come to conclusion that there is disability of 50%.

It is NC: 2023:KHC:20641 also relevant to note that the appellant may go on appearing before the different entities or institutions which may give such similar certificate of the disability at different points of time.
Under these circumstances, this court comes to the conclusion, that such additional documents are not essential for the just decision in the matter.
Under these circumstances, this court feels that the I.A. is not of much relevant at this juncture, when an opportunity was granted to the appellant by the Tribunal to adduce the evidence.
Moreover, it is the evidence of the doctor who treated the petitioner which is of sterling quality and evidence of other doctors who had assessed the disability only is not of much value.
For this reason also, the application cannot be entertained at this stage.
Obviously such application would only put the lis into a reverse gear.

12. Coming to the merits of this case, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that appellant had sustained fracture of Femur of both legs and the NC: 2023:KHC:20641 fracture of femur of left leg has resulted in shortening of 2.5 cms.
He points out that the right femur had certain distortion and it had rotated and it was set right subsequently at the time of the inpatient treatment at yenopoya hospital.
It is submitted that these two fractures of the both the femurs were not properly considered by the Tribunal.
He submits that disability as opined by the CW-1, who had treated the petitioner could not have been brushed aside by the Tribunal to hold that disability was only to the extent of 10%.
It is submitted that the value that could be attached to the testimony of the treated doctor was not at all considered by the Tribunal.
He submit that the say of the doctor who treated the petitioner gains much importance, since no doctor would come forward to say his treatment has resulted in more disability.
I find considerable force in the submission made by the learned counsel for the appellant in this regard.
It is submitted that Tribunal has not awarded compensation under other heads and the compensation awarded is also on the lower side.

He points out that the compensation in respect of M. M. Usman vs K. K. Ibrahim on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56654915/
4 the medical expenses was also not properly dealt by the Tribunal.

14. Further learned counsel for the appellant submits that income of the petitioner was not assessed properly and even though PW-3 was examined, his say was also brushed aside and tribunal has considered income at Rs.7,500/-.
15.

Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent contends that Tribunal has assessed the disability of the petitioner in a proper manner and it has also considered the compensation under the relevant heads.
He points out that some of the medical bills, do not bear the seal and signature of Pharmacist.

It is also submitted that the prescription are also not available, and therefore the compensation awarded by the Tribunal to the tune of Rs.1,00,000/- under the medical head is justified.
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:20641
Regarding disability, he submit that the CW-1 could not have deposed about the functional disability and he could have only deposed about the physical disability.
Hence, he contends that compensation awarded by the tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
So far as the income of the petitioner is concerned, he submit that there is no document to show that the PW-3 was contractor and he used to pay Rs.18,000/- per month as claimed by the petitioner.
Hence he has sought for the dismissal of the appeal.
16. The fact that there was an accident involving the car insured by the respondent no.2-insurance company and the motor cycle of the petitioner is not in dispute.
Further, the fact that the car was covered with the insurance issued by the respondent no.2 is also not in dispute.
Therefore, it is not necessary for this court to enter into those aspects.
17. It is worth to note that the case sheet produced at Ex.C-1 show that petitioner had sustained fracture of - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:20641 the left as well as the right femur.
The evidence of CW-1 is consistent with the notings in the Ex.C-1 case sheet.
It is evident that, petitioner was operated on 17.05.2016 for nailing of right femur and on 19.05.2016 for nailing of left femur and again on 03.06.2016 to restore alignment on the left femur.
Apart from that, he had sustained fracture of the clavicle and ultimately he was discharged on 20.06.2016.
Thus it shows that he was inpatient for more than 45 days.
Obviously, such injuries had left him disabled from his earning at least for a period of six months.
The CW-1 also say he had examined the petitioner and he has found 20% disability which is also attributable to the shortening of the right leg by 2.5 cms.
It is relevant to note that such shortening of leg results in gait.
The petitioner claims that he was a driver and writer and therefore there is functional disability.
Dr. Savith Shetty-CW-1, has assessed the functional disability and it is also 20%.
In other words, he says that physical as well as functional disability is to the extent of 20%.

sentences.text: The Tribunal in his judgment do not offer the reason, as to why the say of the treated doctor is not believable so far as the disability is concerned.
It has simply reduced the disability to 10% from 20%, without giving any reasons.
One can justify such reduction in the disability if the person who had assessed the disability had not treated the injured.
Under these circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries suffered as well as evidence available on record, it is proper to hold petitioner has sustained disability of 20%.
19. So far as, income of the petitioner is concerned, the PW-3 has not produced any documentary evidence to show that he was paying Rs.600/- per day to the petitioner.
He also has not produced any document to show that he was a contractor and had employed workers under him.
If at all he was a contractor, definitely he would have got documents to establish that he was contractor.
In the absence of such documents, it is not - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:20641 possible for this court to hold that petitioner was earning Rs.600/- per day.
20. The guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority prescribe the notional income at Rs.9,500/- per month for the year 2016.
In umpteen number of cases, this court has held that the guidelines issued by KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under Minimum Wages Act for a skilled labourer.
Therefore, the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.9,500/- per month as prescribed under the guidelines is accepted.

Thus the compensation entitled by the appellant under the head of loss of future income is calculated as Rs.9,500/- x 12 x 20% x 17 = Rs.3,87,600/-
by adopting multiplier of 17.
21.
Obviously the petitioner was unable to resume his work for period of six months, on account of fracture of both the femurs.
Hence, petitioner is also entitled for Rs.9,500/- x 6 =Rs.57,000/- under this head.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- under the head of pain and agony.
Obviously it was in respect of fracture of one femur.
Therefore the compensation under the head of pain and suffering is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
23. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head of medical expenses and there was no reason to reduce the medical expenses from Rs.1,50,000/- to Rs.1,00,000/-.
Therefore the medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,50,000/- has to be awarded.

25. The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head of traveling, conveyance and attendance charges and the same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.
26. The CW-1 has stated that the petitioner needs another Rs.20,000/- for future medical expenses.
Therefore the petitioner is also entitled for future medical - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:20641 expenses for Rs.20,000/-.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for a revised compensation under different heads as follows:

Hence, the following order:-
The appeal is allowed-in-part.
